**Quick summary**  

- About **10%** currently vape; about **20%** have ever vaped.  
- About **8%** currently smoke; about **18%** have ever smoked.
- The overall pattern is **broadly similar to the UK**.

:::

## Why This Matters

Vaping and smoking in young people affect health now and into adulthood. Knowing how many young people vape or smoke helps us plan prevention, protect children, and track progress over time. This briefing shares our headline figures from St Helena’s 2025 youth smoking survey. A technical appendix at the end explains the ‘what‑if’ checks we’ve used to be transparent about our uncertainty around these estimates.

## What We Did
In June 2025 we asked students at St Helena’s secondary school to take part in a survey about smoking and vaping. Of the 139 students invited, almost all joined in: 125 answered our key questions on vaping and 123 on smoking. This gives us an 89% response rate, a strong level of participation. Since the school has 196 students in total, our survey reached around seven in ten young people on the island. To work out how common smoking and vaping are, we assumed that the few who did not take part had similar habits to those who did. We also tested this idea by running five different “what if” scenarios, which gave us a range of possible results. This survey provides the best picture yet of youth smoking and vaping on St Helena, helping us understand and address this important health issue.  The full details are explained in the technical appendix.

| Key Messages                                               |                                               |
| ------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Current Vaping**                                        | **Current Smoking**                                       |
| Our best estimate is 10% (between 6% and 15%). <br />That’s about 1 in 10 young people | Our best estimate is 8% (between 4% and 12%). <br />That’s about 1 in 13 young people. |
|  |  |
| **Ever Tried Vaping**                                        | **Ever Tried Smoking**                                       |
| About 20% (between 14% and 27%) have tried a vape at least once. | About 18% (between 13% and 25%) have tried a cigarette at least once. |

## How This Compares With The UK 
St Helena youths report rates of vaping that are roughly the same as in Great Britain, and rates of smoking that are almost twice that of England @ukvaping2024. In Great Britain (ages 11–17): around 7% currently vape and 20% tried vaping at some point @ash2025. In England (ages 11–15): around 3% are current smokers and 11% have ever smoked @nhsdigital2023sdd. Age bands differ slightly, so treat this as a rough comparison rather than a strict like‑for‑like.

#| echo: false
import pandas as pd
import plotly.graph_objects as go

# --- Scenario values (replace with your real numbers) -----------------------
scenario_table = pd.DataFrame([
    ["Main estimate", 10, 20,  8, 18],
    ["Non-responders are NO",  9, 18,  7, 16],
    ["Non-responders are YES",  19, 28, 18, 28],
    ["Non-responders (2×)", 11, 20,  9, 18],
    ["Non-responders (0.5×)",  9, 19,  7, 17],
], columns=["scenario", "vape_current", "vape_ever", "smoke_current", "smoke_ever"])

# UK comparators (from your data dictionary inputs)
uk = {
    "Vaping":  {"current": 7, "ever": 20},
    "Smoking": {"current": 3, "ever": 11},
}

categories = ["Vaping", "Smoking"]  # shown top-to-bottom after axis setup

def scenario_to_segments(row: pd.Series) -> pd.DataFrame:
    data = []
    for cat in categories:
        if cat == "Vaping":
            current = float(row["vape_current"])
            ever = float(row["vape_ever"])
        else:
            current = float(row["smoke_current"])
            ever = float(row["smoke_ever"])

        ever_not_current = max(0.0, ever - current)
        never = max(0.0, 100.0 - ever)
        data.append([cat, current, ever_not_current, never])
    return pd.DataFrame(data, columns=["type", "current", "ever_not_current", "never"])

# --- Colors (approximate your Stata palette) --------------------------------
COL_CURRENT = "#2f4b7c"   # dark blue
COL_EVER    = "#3aa0c8"   # teal-blue
COL_NEVER   = "#cbbf93"   # sand

HALO_LINE   = "rgba(0,0,0,0.25)"  # subtle outline for the white halo

# --- Base data (initial scenario) ------------------------------------------
seg0 = scenario_to_segments(scenario_table.iloc[0])

uk_current_x = [uk[c]["current"] for c in categories]
uk_ever_x    = [uk[c]["ever"]    for c in categories]

fig = go.Figure()

# Stacked bars
fig.add_trace(go.Bar(
    name="Current",
    y=seg0["type"],
    x=seg0["current"],
    orientation="h",
    marker=dict(color=COL_CURRENT, line=dict(width=0)),
    hovertemplate="%{y}<br>Current: %{x:.1f}%<extra></extra>",
))
fig.add_trace(go.Bar(
    name="Ever (not current)",
    y=seg0["type"],
    x=seg0["ever_not_current"],
    orientation="h",
    marker=dict(color=COL_EVER, line=dict(width=0)),
    hovertemplate="%{y}<br>Ever (not current): %{x:.1f}%<extra></extra>",
))
fig.add_trace(go.Bar(
    name="Never",
    y=seg0["type"],
    x=seg0["never"],
    orientation="h",
    marker=dict(color=COL_NEVER, line=dict(width=0)),
    hovertemplate="%{y}<br>Never: %{x:.1f}%<extra></extra>",
))

# UK markers with "floating" halo effect (two traces per set)

# UK Current halo
fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
    name="UK Current",
    y=categories,
    x=uk_current_x,
    mode="markers",
    marker=dict(size=18, color="white", line=dict(width=2, color=HALO_LINE)),
    hovertemplate="%{y}<br>UK Current: %{x:.1f}%<extra></extra>",
    legendgroup="uk_current",
    showlegend=False,
))
# UK Current coloured dot
fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
    name="UK Current",
    y=categories,
    x=uk_current_x,
    mode="markers",
    marker=dict(size=16, color=COL_CURRENT, line=dict(width=0)),
    hovertemplate="%{y}<br>UK Current: %{x:.1f}%<extra></extra>",
    legendgroup="uk_current",
    showlegend=True,
))

# UK Ever halo
fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
    name="UK Ever",
    y=categories,
    x=uk_ever_x,
    mode="markers",
    marker=dict(size=18, color="white", line=dict(width=2, color=HALO_LINE)),
    hovertemplate="%{y}<br>UK Ever: %{x:.1f}%<extra></extra>",
    legendgroup="uk_ever",
    showlegend=False,
))
# UK Ever coloured dot
fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
    name="UK Ever",
    y=categories,
    x=uk_ever_x,
    mode="markers",
    marker=dict(size=16, color=COL_EVER, line=dict(width=0)),
    hovertemplate="%{y}<br>UK Ever: %{x:.1f}%<extra></extra>",
    legendgroup="uk_ever",
    showlegend=True,
))

# --- Layout: fix background, spacing, aspect, overlap -----------------------
fig.update_layout(
    template="simple_white",
    barmode="stack",
    bargap=0.45,  # makes the bars thinner / more airy for 2 categories
    margin=dict(l=80, r=30, t=40, b=80),

    xaxis=dict(
        title="",
        range=[0, 100],
        showgrid=False,
        zeroline=False,
        ticks="outside",
        # domain=[0.28, 1.0],   # ← try 0.05–0.12

    ),
    yaxis=dict(
        title="",
        categoryorder="array",
        categoryarray=categories[::-1],  # so Vaping appears above Smoking
    ),

    # More horizontal room; extra right margin for dropdown + label
    height=420,  # taller = less “fat bar” feel

    paper_bgcolor="white",
    plot_bgcolor="white",

    legend=dict(
        orientation="h",
        x=0.5, y=-0.2,
        xanchor="center", yanchor="top",
        borderwidth=0,
        font=dict(size=18) 
    ),

    # Smooth transitions (used by animation)
    transition=dict(duration=450, easing="cubic-in-out"),
)

# Remove axis lines, ticks, tick labels styling
fig.update_xaxes(
    showline=False,
    ticks="",
    tickvals=[10, 20, 30, 40, 100],
    ticktext=["10", "20", "30", "40", "100"],
    showticklabels=True,          # keep numbers; set False if you want none
    tickfont=dict(size=16),
    title_font=dict(size=18),
)

fig.update_yaxes(
    showline=False,
    ticks="",
    ticklabelposition="outside left",
    showticklabels=False, # keep category labels; set False to hide
    tickfont=dict(size=16),
    title_font=dict(size=18),
    automargin=True
)

fig.add_annotation(
    x=0.75,
    y=0,
    xref="paper",
    yref="paper",
    text="Percentage (%)",
    showarrow=False,
    font=dict(size=20),
    xanchor="center",
    yanchor="top"
)

fig.add_annotation(
    x=-0.01,
    y=0.83,
    xref="paper",
    yref="paper",
    text="Vaping",
    showarrow=False,
    font=dict(size=17),
    xanchor="right",
    yanchor="top"
)
fig.add_annotation(
    x=-0.01,
    y=0.34,
    xref="paper",
    yref="paper",
    text="Smoking",
    showarrow=False,
    font=dict(size=17),
    xanchor="right",
    yanchor="top"
)
fig.add_annotation(
    x=0.15, y=1.3,
    xref="paper", yref="paper",
    text="Scenario:",
    showarrow=False,
    font=dict(size=18),
    xanchor="left",
)


# --- Frames for smooth scenario transitions ---------------------------------
frames = []
for _, row in scenario_table.iterrows():
    seg = scenario_to_segments(row)
    frames.append(go.Frame(
        name=row["scenario"],
        data=[
            go.Bar(x=seg["current"],          y=seg["type"]),
            go.Bar(x=seg["ever_not_current"], y=seg["type"]),
            go.Bar(x=seg["never"],            y=seg["type"]),
            # UK markers unchanged in frames (leave them as-is)
            fig.data[3], fig.data[4], fig.data[5], fig.data[6]
        ]
    ))

fig.frames = frames

# Dropdown with animate
fig.update_layout(
    updatemenus=[dict(
        type="dropdown", 
        direction="down",
        x=0.4, y=1.3,
        xanchor="center", yanchor="top",
        showactive=True,
        buttons=[
            dict(
                label=s,
                method="animate",
                args=[
                    [s],
                    dict(
                        frame=dict(duration=450, redraw=True),
                        transition=dict(duration=450, easing="cubic-in-out"),
                        mode="immediate"
                    )
                ],
            )
            for s in scenario_table["scenario"]
        ],
    )],
)

# fig

## How Confident Are We About These Results?
Our results are based on the youth who took part, but we also tested what might happen if the few non-responders had different smoking or vaping habits. We ran four “what-if” scenarios in addition to our main results. For vaping, this gave overall rates between about 10% and 19%. One scenario—assuming non-responders had slightly higher vaping levels than responders—seems especially plausible, and gave results very close to our main estimate. For smoking, the detailed scenarios are shown in the appendix. Overall, these checks show our findings are reasonably robust—the big picture does not change dramatically when we test different possibilities.


::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

## Technical Appendix

Methods
This survey was conducted in June 2025 among students attending the single secondary school on St Helena. The questionnaire was adapted from the ASH UK Youth Smokefree Survey 2025, which has been used annually across Great Britain, with minor modifications to ensure local relevance. Students completed the survey online during school hours under teacher supervision. Participation was voluntary and anonymous, with no individual identifiers collected. A total of 139 students (71% of the school population) took part, of whom 123 provided valid responses to questions on vaping and 125 on smoking, yielding an overall response rate of 89% of those invited. Prevalence estimates for smoking and vaping were calculated as proportions of valid responses. To address uncertainty arising from non-response, we conducted scenario analyses assuming different patterns of behaviour among non-responders. Results are reported as point estimates with plausible ranges (known as credibility intervals) reflecting these alternative scenarios.

Our ‘What-If’ Scenarios
Our results come from the students who answered the survey, but not everyone took part. To check how much difference that might make, we tested five different “what-if” situations:

1. Main estimate (best guess): We assumed students who didn’t answer were the same as those who did. This gives our headline figures.
2. All non-responders are non-smokers/non-vapers: This gives the lowest possible rates.
3. All non-responders are smokers/vapers: This gives the highest possible rates.
4. Non-responders smoke/vape a bit more than responders (twice the rate of responders): This is a realistic scenario based on other surveys, and the results stayed close to our main estimate.
5. Non-responders smoke/vape a bit less than responders (half the rate of responders): This is also possible, but again did not shift the results much.

| Scenario                                             | Current    Vaping            | Ever  Tried   Vaping | Current    Smoking  | Ever  Tried   Smoking | Interpretation                          |
| ---------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------- | -------------------- | ------------------- | --------------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| Main estimate   (credibility interval)               | 10% (6–15%)                  | 20% (14–27%)         | 8% (4–12%)          | 18% (13–25%)          | Our best estimate – headline results    |
| All non-responders are   non-smokers/non-vapers      | 9% (lowest bound)            | 18%                  | 7% (lowest bound)   | 16%                   | Likely underestimates real use          |
| All non-responders are   smokers/vapers              | 19% (highest bound)          | 28%                  | 18% (highest bound) | 28%                   | Likely overestimates real use           |
| Non-responders smoke/vape a bit more than responders | 11% (close to main estimate) | 20%                  | 9%                  | 18%                   | Plausible – close to best estimate      |
| Non-responders smoke/vape a bit less than responders | 9% (close to main estimate)  | 19%                  | 7%                  | 17%                   | Also plausible – close to best estimate |
